records.source: וְֽ֠הָיָה מִסְפַּ֤ר בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יִמַּ֖ד וְלֹ֣א יִסָּפֵ֑ר וְֽ֠הָיָה בִּמְק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יֵאָמֵ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לֹֽא־עַמִּ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם יֵאָמֵ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י אֵֽל־חָֽי׃
records.gloss: And will be [the] number of [the] sons of Israel like [the] sand of the sea, which not will be measured and not will be counted; and it will be in [the] place where it was said to them, Not my people [are] you, it will be said to them, Sons of [the] God living.
pieces: Yet the number of the people of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which no one can measure or count. In the very place where they were told, "You are not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people," they will be told, "You are {{gender:children|sons}} of the living God."

L.1: And the number of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which will not be measured and will not be counted; and it will be, in the place where it was said to them, "Not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people [are] you," it will be said to them, "{{gender:Children|Sons}} of [the] living God."

R.1: But one day the people of Israel will be as many as the grains of sand by the sea. No one will be able to measure them or count them. In the same place where they were told, "You are not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people," they will be called "{{gender:children|sons}} of the living God."

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew text, 1:10 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 2 here, so that the promise of 2:1-3 opens the new chapter. Many Bibles end chapter 1 with this verse and the next, numbering them 1:10-11, and then begin chapter 2 with "Say to your brothers" (Hebrew 2:3), so their 2:1-23 is 2:3-25 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Hosea is cited that way.

decisions.choice: like the sand of the sea: the promise to Abraham and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham offspring as many as the sand on the seashore (Genesis 22:17) and repeated it to Jacob (Genesis 32:13). Right after the names of judgment, the old promise is restated: the people declared "not my people" will still become countless.

decisions.choice: in the place where: in the same place where they were disowned
decisions.reason: The words usually mean "in the place where". The place may be the land itself, or Jezreel (2:2). The same words can also mean "instead of" (as Isaiah 33:21 uses a similar phrase), giving "instead of being told 'You are not my people', they will be told ...". The sense is close either way: the name of rejection is replaced by a name of belonging.

decisions.choice: Romans 9:26 quotes this verse
decisions.reason: Paul quotes these words, as they stand in the Greek Old Testament, together with 2:25, and applies them to Gentiles whom God has called (Romans 9:24-26). In Hosea the promise is first to Israel, the people who had been named "not my people". The verse is also behind 1 Peter 2:10.

decisions.choice: children of the living God: a name of belonging that replaces "not my people"
decisions.reason: Israel is called the LORD's son (Exodus 4:22; Hosea 11:1) and his children (Deuteronomy 14:1). "The living God" sets him against idols that have no life, the Baals of chapter 2. The word is "sons", which here includes the whole people, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: children / sons (gender setting); people of Israel (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Israel" and "sons of the living God" mean the whole people, so they take the gender setting. Balanced and Readable say "the people of Israel" in the first clause. Literal keeps the Hebrew order "Not my people are you".

records.heading: Children of the living God

records.source: וְ֠נִקְבְּצוּ בְּנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֤ה וּבְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו וְשָׂמ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם רֹ֥אשׁ אֶחָ֖ד וְעָל֣וּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י גָד֖וֹל י֥וֹם יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
records.gloss: And will be gathered [the] sons of Judah and [the] sons of Israel together, and they will appoint for themselves head one, and they will go up from the land, for great [will be the] day of Jezreel.
pieces: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together. They will appoint one leader for themselves and will go up out of the land, for the day of Jezreel will be great.

L.2: And there will be gathered the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel together, and they will set over themselves one head, and they will go up out of the land; because great [will be] the day of Jezreel.

R.2: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will come together again. They will choose one leader for themselves, and they will go up out of the land. The day of Jezreel will be a great day!

decisions.choice: Judah and Israel gathered together under one head: the divided kingdoms reunited
decisions.reason: Israel and Judah had been two kingdoms since the death of Solomon (1 Kings 12). The promise is that they will be one people again under a single leader. The word is "head", not "king"; 3:5 names the king as "David their king". Ezekiel 37:15-24 makes the same promise with two sticks joined into one.

decisions.choice: go up from the land: the sense is uncertain
alternatives: come up out of the land of exile
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read in several ways. (1) They will come up out of the land of their exile, as Israel once came up out of Egypt (2:17). (2) They will spring up from the ground like a crop, which suits the name Jezreel, "God sows" (2:24-25). (3) They will take possession of the land; Exodus 1:10 uses the same words, where Pharaoh fears the Israelites will "go up from the land", with a sense that is itself debated. The translation keeps the Hebrew words, which leave the choice open.

decisions.choice: great will be the day of Jezreel: the name now promises good
decisions.reason: In 1:4-5 Jezreel was a place of bloodshed and defeat. Here "the day of Jezreel" is a day of gathering, and the name's meaning, "God sows", comes to the front: God will plant his people again (2:24-25).

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:2 in the Hebrew text, 1:11 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: See 2:1. Bibles that number this verse 1:11 begin chapter 2 with the next verse.

decisions.choice: appoint one leader (B); choose one leader (R)
decisions.reason: "Head" means a leader here. Balanced and Readable say "leader"; Literal keeps "head". Readable adds "again" to "come together", which the promise implies after the division of the kingdoms (m1).

records.source: אִמְר֥וּ לַאֲחֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּ֑י וְלַאֲחֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם רֻחָֽמָה׃
records.gloss: Say to your brothers, My people, and to your sisters, She is shown compassion.
pieces: Say to your brothers, "My People," \q and to your sisters, "Shown Compassion."

L.3: Say to your brothers, "Ammi," \q and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."

R.3: Call your brothers "My People." \q Call your sisters "Shown Compassion."

decisions.choice: This verse is 2:3 in the Hebrew text, 2:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: Bibles that number Hebrew 2:1-2 as 1:10-11 begin their chapter 2 here, so Hebrew 2:3-25 is their 2:1-23. In the Hebrew, this verse closes the promise of 2:1-2; in those Bibles it opens the speech that follows.

decisions.choice: Ammi, "my people"; Ruhamah, "shown compassion": the children's names without the "not"
decisions.reason: The names Lo-ammi (1:9) and Lo-ruhamah (1:6) return with "not" taken away. Ammi means "my people"; Ruhamah means "she is shown compassion". The reversal promised in 2:1 is put into words the people can say to one another.

decisions.choice: say ... your brothers ... your sisters: the people of Israel are told to call one another by the new names
decisions.reason: "Say" and "your" are plural. The people are addressed, perhaps as the children of the mother of 2:4. Each is to call the others by the names of restored belonging. Some read the verse as the opening of the next section, where the children are told to bring a case against their mother; the Hebrew chapter places it at the end of the promise.

decisions.choice: the new names behind Romans 9:25 and 1 Peter 2:10
decisions.reason: The renaming that begins here is completed in 2:25, the verse Paul quotes in Romans 9:25. 1 Peter 2:10 also uses it: "once not a people, now God's people". See 2:25.

decisions.choice: My People; Shown Compassion (B, R); Ammi; Ruhamah (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable translate the names, as they do Not My People and No Compassion in chapter 1; Literal keeps the Hebrew names with their meaning in the footnote (m2). Readable says "Call" for "Say to", which is what the verse asks.

records.source: רִ֤יבוּ בְאִמְּכֶם֙ רִ֔יבוּ כִּֽי־הִיא֙ לֹ֣א אִשְׁתִּ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֣א אִישָׁ֑הּ וְתָסֵ֤ר זְנוּנֶ֨יהָ֙ מִפָּנֶ֔יהוְנַאֲפוּפֶ֖יהָ מִבֵּ֥ין שָׁדֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Contend with your mother, contend, for she not [is] my wife, and I not [am] her husband; and let her remove her prostitutions from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts,
pieces: Bring a charge against your mother, bring a charge, \q because she is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wife, and I am not her husband. \q She must put away her prostitution from her face \q and her adultery from between her breasts,

L.4: Contend with your mother, contend, \q because she [is] not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wife, and I [am] not her husband, \q and let her remove her prostitutions from her face \q and her adulteries from between her breasts,

R.4: Accuse your mother! Accuse her! \q She is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wife, and I am not her husband. \q She must stop showing herself off as a prostitute \q and giving her body to other men.

decisions.choice: the LORD speaks as the husband; the mother is Israel, the children are her people
decisions.reason: From here to 2:25 the LORD speaks ("declares the LORD", 2:15, 18, 23). Hosea's marriage gives the picture: the LORD is the husband, the nation is the wife and mother, and the people are her children, called to take their stand against their mother's ways. At times the poem speaks of the woman and at times of the land (2:5, 11).

decisions.choice: contend: bring a case against, accuse
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a legal dispute, a charge brought in court (Isaiah 3:13; Micah 6:1-2). The children are called to accuse their mother, joining their father's case against her.

decisions.choice: she is not my wife, and I am not her husband: the marriage is broken by her unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The words sound like a formula of divorce. Yet the aim of what follows is not to end the marriage but to bring the wife back (2:9, 16-22). The sentence states how things stand: by her unfaithfulness she has broken the bond.

decisions.choice: prostitution from her face, adulteries from between her breasts: marks of unfaithfulness on her body
decisions.reason: This may refer to things worn: face paint, jewelry, or tokens of other gods worn on the face and between the breasts (compare Genesis 38:15; Jeremiah 4:30; Hosea 2:15). Or it may be a vivid way of naming the body given to others. Either way she is told to put away all that marks her unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 2:5
decisions.reason: "Let her remove" is followed by "or I will strip her" (2:5): the warning gives the reason for the demand.

decisions.choice: Bring a charge against (B); Accuse (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "contend with". Balanced and Readable give the legal sense (m2).

decisions.choice: She must stop showing herself off as a prostitute and giving her body to other men
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the images of face and breasts stand for (m4) without making them cruder than the Hebrew, as the terms note asks for the marriage chapters. Readable ends the sentence here; 2:5 begins with "If she does not".

records.source: פֶּן־אַפְשִׁיטֶ֣נָּה עֲרֻמָּ֔ה וְהִ֨צַּגְתִּ֔יהָ כְּי֖וֹם הִוָּֽלְדָ֑הּ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣יהָ כַמִּדְבָּ֗ר וְשַׁתִּ֨הָ֙ כְּאֶ֣רֶץ צִיָּ֔ה וַהֲמִתִּ֖יהָ בַּצָּמָֽא׃
records.gloss: Lest I strip her naked and set her as [the] day she was born, and make her like the wilderness, and set her like a land of dryness, and kill her with thirst.
pieces: or I will strip her naked \q and leave her as bare as on the day she was born. \q I will make her like a wilderness, turn her into a parched land, \q and let her die of thirst.

L.5: lest I strip her naked \q and set her [out] as on the day she was born, \q and make her like the wilderness, and set her like a land of drought, \q and kill her with thirst.

R.5: If she does not, I will tear off her clothes \q and leave her as naked as the day she was born. \q I will make her like a desert, like a dry land, \q and she will die of thirst.

decisions.choice: strip her naked: the public shaming of an unfaithful wife
decisions.reason: A husband was to provide his wife's clothing (Exodus 21:10). To strip her is to take back what he gave and to shame her openly, a picture the prophets use for a city's disgrace (Jeremiah 13:26; Ezekiel 16:37-39). "As on the day she was born" recalls the people's beginnings, when they had nothing (compare Ezekiel 16:4-7).

decisions.choice: like the wilderness ... a land of drought ... thirst: the woman pictured as a land without rain
decisions.reason: The image moves from the wife to the land she stands for. The people credited Baal with rain and crops (2:7, 10). The LORD will show who gives them by holding back the rain, until the land is like a desert.

decisions.choice: If she does not
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence with what "lest" means: if she does not put away her unfaithfulness (2:4).

records.source: וְאֶת־בָּנֶ֖יהָ לֹ֣א אֲרַחֵ֑ם כִּֽי־בְנֵ֥י זְנוּנִ֖ים הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And her children not I will have compassion on, for children of prostitutions [are] they.
pieces: I will not show compassion to her children, \q because they are children born of promiscuity.

L.6: And on her children I will not have compassion, \q for they [are] children of prostitution.

R.6: I will not show compassion to her children, \q because they were born of unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: I will not have compassion: the name No Compassion (1:6) applied to all her children
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the daughter's name. What was said through one child's name is now said of all the mother's children: the people as well as the nation.

decisions.choice: children of prostitution: as in 1:2
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the words of the command to Hosea (1:2). The children share their mother's character; the next verse gives the reason.

decisions.choice: children born of promiscuity (B); born of unfaithfulness (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as 1:2 at each level.

records.source: כִּ֤י זָֽנְתָה֙ אִמָּ֔ם הֹבִ֖ישָׁה הֽוֹרָתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמְרָ֗ה אֵלְכָ֞ה אַחֲרֵ֤י מְאַהֲבַי֙ נֹתְנֵ֤י לַחְמִי֙ וּמֵימַ֔י צַמְרִ֣י וּפִשְׁתִּ֔י שַׁמְנִ֖י וְשִׁקּוּיָֽי׃
records.gloss: For has prostituted herself their mother; has acted shamefully she who conceived them; for she said, I will go after my lovers, [who] give my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drinks.
pieces: Their mother has prostituted herself; \q she who conceived them has behaved shamefully. \q For she said, "I will follow my lovers, who give me my food and water, \q my wool and flax, \q my oil and drink."

L.7: For their mother has prostituted herself; \q she who conceived them has acted shamefully. \q For she said, "Let me go after my lovers, givers of my bread and my water, \q my wool and my flax, \q my oil and my drinks."

R.7: Their mother has been unfaithful. \q She has done shameful things. \q She said, "I will go after my lovers. They give me my food and my water, \q my wool and linen, \q my olive oil and my drinks."

decisions.choice: my lovers: the Baals, the gods she thinks give her food and clothing
decisions.reason: The lovers are named in 2:15 and 2:19 as the Baals, the local forms of the Canaanite storm god, who was worshiped as the giver of rain and crops. Hosea also uses the language of lovers for Israel's turning to foreign powers for help (8:9). Here the gifts she names, food, water, wool, flax, oil and drink, are the gifts of the land, and 2:10 answers that it was the LORD who gave them.

decisions.choice: acted shamefully: behaved in a way that brings disgrace
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for shame. It means more than feeling ashamed: she has done what disgraces her and her children.

decisions.choice: my bread ... my drinks: she calls the gifts her own
decisions.reason: Six times she says "my". In 2:11 the LORD answers with "my grain ... my new wine ... my wool and my flax": the gifts were his, given to her.

decisions.choice: food (B, R); linen (R); olive oil (R)
decisions.reason: "Bread" means food in general here, and Balanced and Readable say "food". Balanced says "my" once for each pair, as English does; Literal repeats it as the Hebrew does. Flax is the plant linen is made from, and the oil is olive oil; Readable uses the words a reader knows.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִי־שָׂ֥ךְ אֶת־דַּרְכֵּ֖ךְ בַּסִּירִ֑ים וְגָֽדַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־גְּדֵרָ֔הּ וּנְתִיבוֹתֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א תִמְצָֽא׃
records.gloss: Therefore here I [am] hedging up your way with thorns, and I will wall up her wall, and her paths not she will find.
pieces: Therefore I will block your way with thorns, \q and I will wall her in, \q so that she cannot find her paths.

L.8: Therefore, look, I am hedging up your way with thorns, \q and I will build up her wall, \q and she will not find her paths.

R.8: So I will block her road with thorn bushes. \q I will build a wall around her, \q so that she cannot find her way.

decisions.choice: your way: the LORD turns for a moment to speak to the woman herself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "your way" (addressed to a woman) and then goes on with "her wall" and "her paths". Such changes of person are common in the prophets. The Greek translation has "her way", making the verse consistent; the Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: hedge your way with thorns, wall her in: stop her from reaching her lovers
decisions.reason: Thorn hedges and stone walls kept animals in fields and travelers on the road. To block a way is to make it impossible to go on (Job 19:8; Lamentations 3:7, 9). The LORD will stop her from reaching her lovers, and so bring her to turn back (2:9).

decisions.choice: her road
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the woman in the third person through the verse, so that the reader does not think someone else is meant by "your" (m1). The person spoken about is the same; only the sudden turn to address her is not reproduced.

records.source: וְרִדְּפָ֤ה אֶת־מְאַהֲבֶ֨יהָ֙ וְלֹֽא־תַשִּׂ֣יג אֹתָ֔ם וּבִקְשָׁ֖תַם וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָ֑א וְאָמְרָ֗ה אֵלְכָ֤ה וְאָשׁ֨וּבָה֙ אֶל־אִישִׁ֣י הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לִ֛י אָ֖ז מֵעָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: And she will pursue her lovers and not she will overtake them, and she will seek them and not she will find; and she will say, I will go and I will return to my husband the first, for [it was] good for me then more than now.
pieces: She will chase after her lovers but not catch them; \q she will look for them but not find them. \q Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, \q for I was better off then than now."

L.9: And she will pursue her lovers, but she will not overtake them; \q and she will seek them, but she will not find [them]. \q And she will say, "Let me go and return to my husband, the first, \q for [it was] better for me then than now."

R.9: She will run after her lovers, but she will not catch them. \q She will look for them, but she will not find them. \q Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband. \q I was better off then than I am now."

decisions.choice: my first husband: the LORD, who took Israel as his own when he brought them out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The first husband is the LORD (2:4, 17-18). The law did not allow a woman to go back to her first husband once she had belonged to another man (Deuteronomy 24:1-4), and Jeremiah 3:1 asks whether Israel can return. Here the LORD himself is preparing the way back.

decisions.choice: for it was better for me then than now: a return driven by need
decisions.reason: Her reason is her own comfort: life was better with her husband. It is a first step, not yet the love of 2:16-22. The LORD uses her need to bring her back.

decisions.choice: pursue ... seek: she chases her lovers eagerly
decisions.reason: "Pursue" is a strong verb, used for hunting or chasing an enemy. "Seek" is the verb used for seeking God (3:5; 5:15). She puts into her lovers the effort that belongs to seeking the LORD.

records.source: וְהִיא֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְעָ֔ה כִּ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔הּ הַדָּגָ֖ן וְהַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֑ר וְכֶ֨סֶף הִרְבֵּ֥יתִי לָ֛הּ וְזָהָ֖ב עָשׂ֥וּ לַבָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And she not knew that I gave to her the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and silver I multiplied for her, and gold [which] they made for Baal.
pieces: She did not acknowledge \q that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil, \q and who lavished on her the silver and gold that they used for Baal.

L.10: And she did not know \q that I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} gave her the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, \q and multiplied for her silver, and gold [that] they made for Baal.

R.10: She did not understand \q that I was the one who gave her the grain, the wine, and the olive oil. \q I gave her more and more silver and gold, but they used it for Baal.

decisions.choice: she did not know: she did not acknowledge the giver
decisions.reason: In Hosea "know" often means to recognize and honor someone in a relationship, not just to have information (4:1, 6; 6:6). She knew where her food came from in fact, but did not acknowledge that it came from the LORD. The promise of 2:22 answers this: "you will know the LORD".

decisions.choice: the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil: the three chief harvests of the land
decisions.reason: These three stand for all the produce of the land and are named together in the covenant blessings (Deuteronomy 7:13; 11:14). The new wine is the juice of the grape harvest, the fresh oil the olive harvest.

decisions.choice: gold they made for Baal: used for Baal, or made into images of Baal
decisions.reason: The words are short: "gold they made for Baal". They may mean that the people offered silver and gold in Baal's worship, or that they made it into images, as 8:4 and 13:2 say they made idols of their silver and gold. "They" is the people whom the woman stands for.

decisions.choice: acknowledge (B); understand (R); lavished (B); more and more (R); used (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "acknowledge" for the sense of "know" here (m1); Readable says "understand". "Multiplied" is "lavished" at Balanced and "more and more" at Readable. Balanced and Readable say "used for Baal", which covers both readings of m3.

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן אָשׁ֔וּב וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י דְגָנִי֙ בְּעִתּ֔וֹ וְתִירוֹשִׁ֖י בְּמֽוֹעֲד֑וֹ וְהִצַּלְתִּי֙ צַמְרִ֣י וּפִשְׁתִּ֔י לְכַסּ֖וֹת אֶת־עֶרְוָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore I will return and I will take my grain in its time and my new wine in its season, and I will snatch away my wool and my flax, to cover her nakedness.
pieces: So I will take back my grain at harvest time \q and my new wine in its season. \q I will snatch away my wool and my flax, \q which were to cover her nakedness.

L.11: Therefore I will turn back and take my grain in its time \q and my new wine in its appointed time, \q and I will snatch away my wool and my flax, \q [given] to cover her nakedness.

R.11: So I will take back my grain and my wine \q when it is time to harvest them. \q I will take away my wool and my linen \q that I gave her to cover her naked body.

decisions.choice: I will return and take: I will take back
decisions.reason: "Return" before another verb often means doing it again or doing it in reverse. Here it means taking back what was given.

decisions.choice: my grain, my new wine, my wool, my flax: the LORD claims the gifts she called hers
decisions.reason: The words answer her claim in 2:7, "my bread ... my wool and my flax". The gifts belonged to the LORD, who gave them.

decisions.choice: in its time, in its season: at harvest, just when she expects it
decisions.reason: The harvest will fail at the very time it should come in. The words show that the LORD rules the seasons, which the people credited to Baal.

decisions.choice: linen (R); her naked body (R); that I gave her (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "linen" for flax, as in 2:7, and makes plain that the LORD had given the wool and flax to clothe her.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֛ה אֲגַלֶּ֥ה אֶת־נַבְלֻתָ֖הּ לְעֵינֵ֣י מְאַהֲבֶ֑יהָ וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹֽא־יַצִּילֶ֥נָּה מִיָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now I will uncover her shamelessness to [the] eyes of her lovers, and anyone not will deliver her from my hand.
pieces: Now I will lay bare her lewdness before her lovers' eyes, \q and no one will rescue her from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

L.12: And now I will uncover her shamelessness before the eyes of her lovers, \q and no one will deliver her from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

R.12: Now I will show her shame to her lovers, \q and no one will be able to rescue her from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: her shamelessness: her shameful, exposed body; the exact sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The noun is found only here. It is related to a word for a foolish or worthless person and perhaps to a word for something withered. It seems to mean her shame, her body stripped bare (as 2:5), or her lewd conduct. The overall sense is clear: her disgrace will be laid open before the lovers she trusted.

decisions.choice: no one will deliver her from my hand: her lovers cannot protect her
decisions.reason: The lovers will watch and do nothing (2:9). Being "in the hand" of someone means being in his power.

records.source: וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ כָּל־מְשׂוֹשָׂ֔הּ חַגָּ֖הּ חָדְשָׁ֣הּ וְשַׁבַּתָּ֑הּ וְכֹ֖ל מוֹעֲדָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And I will put an end to all her joy, her festival, her new moon and her sabbath, and every appointed feast of hers.
pieces: I will put an end to all her celebrations, \q her festivals, her new moons, and her Sabbaths, \q and all her appointed feasts.

L.13: And I will put an end to all her joy, \q her festival, her new moon, and her Sabbath, \q and all her appointed feasts.

R.13: I will put a stop to all her celebrations: \q her yearly festivals, her new moon feasts, her Sabbath days, \q and all her other holy days.

decisions.choice: festival, new moon, Sabbath, appointed feast: Israel's yearly, monthly and weekly holy days
decisions.reason: The festivals were the three pilgrimage feasts of the year (Exodus 23:14-17). The new moon began each month with offerings (Numbers 28:11). The Sabbath was the weekly day of rest. "Appointed feasts" covers all the holy days the law set (Leviticus 23). Isaiah 1:13-14 lists the same days.

decisions.choice: her festivals: the feasts have become hers, not the LORD's
decisions.reason: The law calls them "the appointed feasts of the LORD" (Leviticus 23:2). Here every one is "hers": they have become occasions of her own pleasure, mixed with the worship of the Baals (2:15).

decisions.choice: celebrations (B, R); yearly festivals, new moon feasts, Sabbath days, other holy days (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses singular nouns for each kind of feast; Balanced and Readable use plurals, since all of them are meant. Readable says what each kind of day is (m1).

records.source: וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִ֗י גַּפְנָהּ֙ וּתְאֵ֣נָתָ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמְרָ֗ה אֶתְנָ֥ה הֵ֨מָּה֙ לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽתְנוּ־לִ֖י מְאַֽהֲבָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֣ים לְיַ֔עַר וַאֲכָלָ֖תַם חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will lay waste her vine and her fig tree, of which she said, Wages [are] they for me, which gave to me my lovers; and I will make them into a thicket, and will eat them [the] animal of the field.
pieces: I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, \q of which she said, "These are my pay, which my lovers gave me." \q I will turn them into a thicket, \q and the wild animals will eat them up.

L.14: And I will lay waste her vine and her fig tree, \q of which she said, "They [are] my wages, which my lovers have given me"; \q and I will make them a thicket, \q and the beasts of the field will eat them.

R.14: I will destroy her grapevines and her fig trees. \q She said, "These are what my lovers paid me." \q I will turn them into a thicket, \q and wild animals will eat them.

decisions.choice: wages: a prostitute's pay
decisions.reason: The word is used for the fee paid to a prostitute (compare 9:1; Deuteronomy 23:19; Micah 1:7). It sounds like the word for "fig tree" in the same verse: the fig trees she counts as her fee will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: vine and fig tree: a picture of peace and plenty
decisions.reason: To sit under one's own vine and fig tree was the picture of a settled, prosperous life (1 Kings 5:5; Micah 4:4). Their ruin means the end of that life.

decisions.choice: a thicket ... the animals of the field: cultivated land going wild
decisions.reason: Untended vineyards and orchards become overgrown, and wild animals feed in them (Isaiah 5:5-6; 7:23-25). In 2:20 the LORD makes a covenant with the same animals for his people's safety.

decisions.choice: my pay (B); what my lovers paid me (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "wages". Balanced and Readable use "pay", which brings out the payment for her favors (m1) without making the wording cruder than the Hebrew.

records.source: וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י עָלֶ֗יהָ אֶת־יְמֵ֤י הַבְּעָלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּקְטִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם וַתַּ֤עַד נִזְמָהּ֙ וְחֶלְיָתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֣י מְאַהֲבֶ֑יהָ וְאֹתִ֥י שָׁכְחָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I will visit on her [the] days of the Baals, when she burned offerings to them, and she adorned herself [with] her ring and her jewelry, and she went after her lovers, and me she forgot, declaration of Yahweh.
pieces: I will punish her for the feast days of the Baals, when she burned offerings to them, \q put on her rings and her jewelry, \q and went after her lovers, \q but forgot {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: And I will visit on her the days of the Baals, when she burned offerings to them, \q and adorned herself with her ring and her jewelry, \q and she went after her lovers; \q but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} she forgot, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: I will punish her for all the times she burned offerings to the Baals. \q She put on her rings and her jewelry \q and went after her lovers. \q But she forgot {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Baals: the many local forms of the god Baal
decisions.reason: Baal, "lord" or "master", was the Canaanite storm god, believed to bring rain and fertility. He was worshiped at many shrines, each with its own Baal, so the Bible often speaks of "the Baals" (Judges 2:11; Jeremiah 2:23). "The days of the Baals" are their festival days, which had replaced the LORD's (2:13).

decisions.choice: burned offerings: made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke. It is used for burning incense and for burning parts of sacrifices on the altar. Either may be meant here; both were part of the worship of the Baals.

decisions.choice: ring: a nose ring or an earring
decisions.reason: The word is used for both (Genesis 24:47; Exodus 32:2). She adorns herself to meet her lovers, as a woman for a feast.

decisions.choice: me she forgot: "me" stands first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "me" first: of all things, the LORD is the one she forgot. Forgetting the LORD is the failure the covenant warned of (Deuteronomy 8:11-19).

decisions.choice: punish (B, R); feast days (B)
decisions.reason: "Visit on her" means to punish her for (as 1:4). Literal keeps "visit". Balanced says "feast days" for "days", since the days of the Baals are their festivals (m1). "Declares the LORD" is "says the LORD" at Readable, as set for the prophets.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מְפַתֶּ֔יהָ וְהֹֽלַכְתִּ֖יהָ הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְדִבַּרְתִּ֖י עַללִבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore here I [am] alluring her, and I will lead her into the wilderness, and I will speak to her heart.
pieces: Therefore I am going to woo her; \q I will lead her into the wilderness \q and speak tenderly to her.

L.16: Therefore, look, I am going to allure her, \q and I will lead her into the wilderness, \q and I will speak to her heart.

R.16: So now I will win her back. \q I will lead her into the desert \q and speak lovingly to her.

decisions.choice: allure: persuade, win over
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade or entice, sometimes to deceive. It is used of a man winning a young woman (Exodus 22:15), and Jeremiah uses it when he says the LORD persuaded him (Jeremiah 20:7). Here the LORD sets out to win his wife's heart again.

decisions.choice: into the wilderness: back to where the covenant began
decisions.reason: The wilderness was where the LORD led Israel after the exodus and made his covenant with them, the time of first love (Jeremiah 2:2). After the barrenness threatened in 2:5, the wilderness here is a place of new beginning. 2:17 makes the link to Egypt explicit.

decisions.choice: speak to her heart: speak tenderly, to comfort and win her
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for a man speaking to win a woman (Genesis 34:3), for kind words that comfort (Ruth 2:13), and for the LORD's comfort to Jerusalem (Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: woo (B); win her back (R); speak tenderly (B); speak lovingly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the verb and the idiom mean here (m1, m3). Literal keeps "allure" and "speak to her heart". The word "look" (Literal) is the usual rendering of the Hebrew word that calls attention; Balanced and Readable leave it out.

records.heading: Led back into the wilderness

records.source: וְנָתַ֨תִּי לָ֤הּ אֶת־כְּרָמֶ֨יהָ֙ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְאֶת־עֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְפֶ֣תַח תִּקְוָ֑ה וְעָ֤נְתָה שָּׁ֨מָּה֙ כִּימֵ֣י נְעוּרֶ֔יהָ וִּכְי֖וֹםעֲלֹתָ֥הּ מֵאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And I will give to her her vineyards from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she will answer there as [in the] days of her youth, and as [the] day of her coming up from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: There I will give her back her vineyards \q and make the valley of Achor a door of hope. \q There she will respond as in the days of her youth, \q as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.

L.17: And I will give her her vineyards from there, \q and the valley of Achor as a door of hope; \q and she will answer there as in the days of her youth, \q and as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.

R.17: There I will give her vineyards back to her. \q I will make the valley of Achor, whose name means trouble, a doorway of hope. \q There she will respond to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as she did when she was young, \q when she came out of the land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the valley of Achor: "the valley of trouble", made a door of hope
decisions.reason: Achor means "trouble". The valley got its name when Achan was punished there for taking what was devoted to the LORD, the first sin after Israel entered the land (Joshua 7:24-26). The place that recalled trouble at the entrance to the land becomes an entrance of hope. Isaiah 65:10 also promises the valley of Achor as a place of rest.

decisions.choice: answer: respond to the LORD's wooing
decisions.reason: The verb most often means "answer" or "respond", which suits the LORD speaking to her heart (2:16) and the chain of answering in 2:23-24. A verb with the same letters means "sing" (Exodus 15:21; 32:18), and some read "she will sing there", as Israel sang after crossing the sea. The sense "respond" is taken here.

decisions.choice: the days of her youth, the day she came up from Egypt: Israel's first love
decisions.reason: The exodus and the wilderness journey are pictured as the time of Israel's youth and engagement to the LORD (Jeremiah 2:2; Ezekiel 16:8). The return to the wilderness (2:16) will be a new exodus.

decisions.choice: from there: once she is there in the wilderness
decisions.reason: "From there" may mean "from that place" (as she comes from the wilderness into the land) or "from that time on". Either way the gifts come after the LORD has brought her into the wilderness.

decisions.choice: There ... back (B, R); respond (B, R); to me (R); whose name means trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "There" for "from there" and "back", since the vineyards were hers before (2:14). They say "respond" for "answer", and Readable adds "to me", the one she responds to. Readable gives the meaning of Achor in the text, which the footnote gives at the other levels (m1).

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה תִּקְרְאִ֖י אִישִׁ֑י וְלֹֽא־תִקְרְאִי־לִ֥י ע֖וֹד בַּעְלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, declaration of Yahweh, you will call, My husband, and not you will call to me again, My baal.
pieces: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you will call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My husband"; \q you will no longer call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My Baal."

L.18: And it will be on that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [that] you will call, "My husband," \q and you will no longer call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "My baal."

R.18: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you will call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My husband." \q You will never again call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My Baal," which means "My master."

decisions.choice: My husband, not My baal: a play on the name of Baal
decisions.reason: Hebrew had two common words a wife could use for her husband: *ish*, "man, husband", and *baal*, "master, owner, husband". The second is also the name of the god Baal. The LORD says that his wife will call him *ishi*, "my husband", and no longer *baali*, "my master" or "my Baal". The word must not be used for him, because it would blur the LORD with Baal, and because the relationship will be one of closeness, not ownership.

decisions.choice: baal may have been used of the LORD himself
decisions.reason: Some Israelites of this period gave their children names with "baal" in them, such as Eshbaal, Saul's son (1 Chronicles 8:33), and Bealiah, one of David's men (1 Chronicles 12:6), whose name means "the LORD is master". Calling the LORD "my baal" may have seemed harmless, but it opened the way to confusing him with Baal. The next verse removes the name altogether.

decisions.choice: you will call: the LORD now speaks to his wife directly
decisions.reason: The verbs are addressed to a woman. After speaking about her in the third person, the LORD turns to her, as he did for a moment in 2:8.

decisions.choice: My baal (L); My Baal (B, R); which means "My master" (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the play by keeping the word baal, as the terms note asks. Literal writes it in lowercase as an ordinary word; Balanced and Readable capitalize it, so the reader sees the god's name; Readable adds what the word means. The footnote explains it (m1). Literal does not supply "me" after the first "call", which the Hebrew leaves out; Balanced and Readable supply it.

records.source: וַהֲסִרֹתִ֛י אֶת־שְׁמ֥וֹת הַבְּעָלִ֖ים מִפִּ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא־יִזָּכְר֥וּ ע֖וֹד בִּשְׁמָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will remove [the] names of the Baals from her mouth, and not they will be remembered again by their name.
pieces: I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, \q and they will no longer be invoked by name.

L.19: And I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, \q and they will no longer be remembered by their name.

R.19: I will take the names of the Baals out of her mouth. \q No one will ever call on them by name again.

decisions.choice: remove the names of the Baals: the command of Exodus 23:13 fulfilled
decisions.reason: The law said: "Make no mention of the names of other gods; let them not be heard on your lips" (Exodus 23:13). What Israel failed to keep, the LORD will bring about himself. Zechariah 13:2 makes a similar promise.

decisions.choice: be remembered by their name: be called on in worship
decisions.reason: To "remember" or "mention" a god's name is to invoke it in prayer, oaths and praise (Joshua 23:7; Psalm 20:8). The Baals will be forgotten in worship.

decisions.choice: invoked (B); call on (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "remembered by name" means here (m2).

records.source: וְכָרַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם בְּרִית֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עִם־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְעִם־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְרֶ֖מֶשׂ הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה וְקֶ֨שֶׁת וְחֶ֤רֶב וּמִלְחָמָה֙ אֶשְׁבּ֣וֹר מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִשְׁכַּבְתִּ֖ים לָבֶֽטַח׃
records.gloss: And I will make for them a covenant in the day the that with [the] animal of the field and with [the] bird of the heavens and [the] creeping thing of the ground; and bow and sword and battle I will break from the land, and I will make them lie down in security.
pieces: On that day I will make a covenant on their behalf \q with the wild animals and the birds of the sky \q and the creatures that move along the ground. \q I will break bow and sword and battle and remove them from the land, \q and I will let them lie down in safety.

L.20: And I will make for them a covenant on that day \q with the beast of the field and with the bird of the sky \q and the creeping thing of the ground; \q and bow and sword and battle I will shatter from the land, \q and I will make them lie down in security.

R.20: At that time I will make an agreement for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people \q with the wild animals and the birds \q and the creatures that crawl on the ground. \q I will put an end to bows and swords and war in the land, \q so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people can lie down and be safe.

decisions.choice: a covenant with the animals, birds and creeping things: creation at peace with God's people
decisions.reason: The three groups are the living creatures of the creation story (Genesis 1:30) and of God's covenant after the flood (Genesis 9:9-10). The animals that were to devour the vineyards (2:14) will no longer threaten. Leviticus 26:6 and Ezekiel 34:25 promise the same: harmful beasts removed and the people living safely.

decisions.choice: bow and sword and battle I will break: 1:5 reversed
decisions.reason: In 1:5 the LORD broke Israel's bow in defeat. Here he breaks the weapons of war themselves, so that no one can attack his people. Compare Psalm 46:10; Isaiah 2:4.

decisions.choice: for them ... make them lie down: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "Them" is the people the woman stands for. The covenant is made by the LORD on their behalf with the animals. "Lie down in security" is the language of the covenant blessing (Leviticus 26:5-6).

decisions.choice: break ... and remove them from the land (B); put an end to ... in the land (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "break from the land", joining two ideas in one verb. Balanced keeps "break" and adds "remove"; Readable says what both mean together.

decisions.choice: my people (R); agreement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as "my people" (m3) and says "agreement" for "covenant", as a plain word for a binding promise.

records.source: וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִ֖י לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִי֙ בְּצֶ֣דֶק וּבְמִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּבְחֶ֖סֶד וּֽבְרַחֲמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will betroth you to me forever; and I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in justice and in covenant loyalty and in compassion.
pieces: I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} forever. \q I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with righteousness and justice, \q with loyal love and compassion.

L.21: And I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} forever; \q and I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in righteousness and in justice, \q and in loyal love and in compassion.

R.21: I will make you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bride forever. \q I will make you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bride, and I will bring to our marriage what is right and fair, \q faithful love and compassion.

decisions.choice: betroth: bind as a wife in the agreement that begins a marriage
decisions.reason: Betrothal was the binding agreement made before a couple lived together, sealed by a payment to the bride's family (Deuteronomy 22:23-29; 2 Samuel 3:14). It was as binding as marriage. The LORD does not simply take back a wife who has been unfaithful; he begins again as if with a young bride, and "forever" means there will be no breaking of this bond. The verb is said three times (2:21-22).

decisions.choice: in righteousness and justice, loyal love and compassion: the bride-price the LORD pays, and the way he will keep the marriage
decisions.reason: The small word translated "in" or "with" is the one used for the price paid for a bride in 2 Samuel 3:14. Read that way, these qualities are the gifts the LORD gives as the bride-price. They also describe the kind of husband he will be. Both senses fit, and the translation keeps the simple "in" at Literal and "with" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: loyal love (*hesed*) and compassion: the covenant love that keeps faith, and tender mercy
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the faithful love that keeps a commitment. Compassion is the word in the daughter's name No Compassion (1:6): what was withheld is now given as a wedding gift.

decisions.choice: make you my bride (R); bring to our marriage what is right and fair (R); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "make you my bride" for "betroth", which is not a common word today. It says "bring to our marriage" so as to keep both senses of m2, and "what is right and fair" for righteousness and justice. *Hesed* is "faithful love" at Readable, as set for the prophets.

records.source: וְאֵרַשְׂתִּ֥יךְ לִ֖י בֶּאֱמוּנָ֑ה וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you will know Yahweh.
pieces: I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with faithfulness, \q and you will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: And I will betroth you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in faithfulness, \q and you will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.22: I will make you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bride, and I will be faithful to you, \q and you will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: the LORD's steady reliability
decisions.reason: The word means firmness, reliability, keeping one's word. It is the third gift of the betrothal: the LORD will be utterly dependable.

decisions.choice: you will know the LORD: you will acknowledge him and live in close relationship with him
decisions.reason: This answers 2:10, "she did not know that I gave her the grain". In Hosea, knowing the LORD means recognizing him, trusting him, and living by his covenant (4:1, 6; 6:3, 6). The word is also used for the closeness of husband and wife, which suits the marriage picture.

decisions.choice: make you my bride, and I will be faithful to you
decisions.reason: Readable says "make you my bride", as in 2:21, and turns "in faithfulness" into a statement of what the LORD will be (m1).

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אֶֽעֱנֶה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה אֶעֱנֶ֖ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְהֵ֖ם יַעֲנ֥וּ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day the that, I will answer, declaration of Yahweh, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
pieces: On that day I will answer, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will answer the heavens, \q and they will answer the earth.

L.23: And it will be on that day [that] I will answer, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I will answer the heavens, \q and they will answer the earth.

R.23: At that time I will answer, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will answer the sky, \q and the sky will answer the earth.

decisions.choice: a chain of answers: the LORD answers the sky, the sky answers the earth with rain
decisions.reason: The verse begins a chain that runs to 2:24: the LORD answers the heavens, the heavens give rain to the earth, the earth gives grain, wine and oil, and these answer Jezreel, the people. Each one responds to the need of the next. The rain and harvest that the people sought from Baal (2:7, 10) come from the LORD.

decisions.choice: answer (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb "answer" is kept at every level through 2:23-24, so that the chain can be seen. Readable says "sky" for "heavens" and repeats "the sky" for "they".

records.source: וְהָאָ֣רֶץ תַּעֲנֶ֔ה אֶת־הַדָּגָ֖ן וְאֶת־הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְאֶת־הַיִּצְהָ֑ר וְהֵ֖ם יַעֲנ֥וּ אֶֽת־יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃
records.gloss: And the earth will answer the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
pieces: The earth will answer the grain, the new wine, and the olive oil, \q and they will answer Jezreel.

L.24: And the earth will answer the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, \q and they will answer Jezreel.

R.24: The earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the olive oil, \q and they will answer Jezreel, the people God plants.

decisions.choice: Jezreel: "God sows", now a name of blessing for the people
decisions.reason: In 1:4 Jezreel named a place of bloodshed. Here it names the people as those whom God sows like seed, and the next verse continues the picture: "I will sow her for myself in the land". The harvest answers them.

decisions.choice: the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil: the gifts of 2:10 restored
decisions.reason: The same three gifts the woman did not know came from the LORD (2:10), and that he took back (2:11), are given again.

decisions.choice: the people God plants
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name in the text, since it carries the promise and leads into 2:25 (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the name with a footnote.

records.source: וּזְרַעְתִּ֤יהָ לִּי֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־לֹ֣א רֻחָ֑מָה וְאָמַרְתִּ֤י לְלֹֽא־עַמִּי֙ עַמִּי־אַ֔תָּה וְה֖וּא יֹאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-ammi, My people [are] you, and he will say, My God.
pieces: I will sow her for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} in the land. \q I will have compassion on No Compassion, \q and I will say to Not My People, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people," \q and he will say, "You are my God."

L.25: And I will sow her for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} in the land, \q and I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, \q and I will say to Lo-ammi, "My people [are] you," \q and he will say, "My God."

R.25: I will plant her in the land for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. \q I will show compassion to No Compassion. \q I will say to Not My People, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people." \q And he will say, "You are my God."

decisions.choice: I will sow her: a play on the name Jezreel, "God sows"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the name Jezreel (2:24). "Her" is the woman of the poem, the people, planted in the land like seed that will grow. Jeremiah 31:27 uses the same picture of sowing the house of Israel.

decisions.choice: Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi: the names of 1:6 and 1:9, now reversed
decisions.reason: The daughter named "Not Shown Compassion" receives compassion, and the son named "Not My People" is told "You are my people". The names stay, but what they said is undone.

decisions.choice: Romans 9:25 and 1 Peter 2:10 use this promise
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse, freely, in Romans 9:25, in the form "I will call those who were not my people 'my people,' and her who was not loved 'loved'". His wording follows the Greek Old Testament, which here has "loved" in some copies where the Hebrew has "shown compassion", and he applies the promise to Gentiles as well as Jews. 1 Peter 2:10 speaks to believers in the words of this verse: once not a people and not shown mercy, now God's people and shown mercy. In Hosea the promise is first spoken to Israel.

decisions.choice: you are my people ... my God: the covenant words restored
decisions.reason: 1:9 denied both halves of the covenant promise (Leviticus 26:12). Here both are spoken again, the LORD's "my people" and the people's answer "my God". Zechariah 13:9 ends with the same exchange.

decisions.choice: No Compassion; Not My People (B, R); Lo-ruhamah; Lo-ammi (L)
decisions.reason: The names are translated at Balanced and Readable and kept in Hebrew at Literal, as in chapter 1. Balanced and Readable supply "You are" before "my God", which the Hebrew leaves out.

decisions.choice: plant
decisions.reason: Readable says "plant" for "sow", a word it uses for seeds and young plants alike, and keeps the link to "the people God plants" in 2:24.
